runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$11.05** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator via `tools/run.py`, flagged). Shares **35,800,000**, one class (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27, `0000041719-26-000049`, checked against issued shares with no treasury line); cap about $395.6M. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-16). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (`0000041719-25-000110`, adverse auditor's opinion on internal control), the 10-Q above, the 8-K of 2026-08-06 (`0001140361-26-031690`), the proxy of 2026-01-14 (`0001140361-26-001150`), the deal prospectus 424B3 of 2024-09-19 (`0001104659-24-101145`, the Treasure carve-out FY2021 to FY2023), Glatfelter's 2023 10-K and its 10-K and 10-Q XBRL 2013 to 2024, Berry Global's 10-Ks FY2016, FY2018, FY2020, FY2021 and FY2024 (the Health, Hygiene & Specialties segment), Mativ's 10-K XBRL. Cross-checks: long-term debt $1,952M at 2025-09-27 against the filed balance sheet; Treasure FY2024 sales plus Glatfelter's twelve months to September 2024 give $3,496.2M against the filer's pro forma $3,496M. `tools/run.py` mixed Glatfelter's and Treasure's years under one CIK; its owner-earnings mean was not used. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (five, listed in the run file). Rivals: the 10-K names six; Mativ the only SEC filer, read; Ahlstrom, Avgol, PFNonwovens, Freudenberg and Fitesa flagged as not SEC filers. **Q1 IN** (nonwoven roll goods for a few large consumer-product makers, top customer 14%, top ten 42%; profit set by volume and the lagged price-cost pass-through). **Q2 OUT** **[L2007-004]**, **[M2013-052]**, **[L2004-003]**, **[M2017-009]**, **[M2012-106]**, **[L2000-017]**, **[M1997-010]**: Americas 83% of five-year segment profit decides; organic volume down five years running (-3%, -8%, -1%, -2%, -1%), FY2025 losses to "competitive pressures from imports in South America"; the FY2022 price-cost gap cost $157M of operating income, operating income 353, 172, 69, 31 before a $172M impairment; customers "could shift suppliers quickly" on the 10-K's own words; Berry's predecessor segment about 8% of sales over FY2016 to FY2024, 3.0% at the trough, Glatfelter 5.9% falling to 0.2%, Mativ 0.3% to 2.4% before write-offs of $401M and $412M, Magnera 0.2% in FY2025 and 2.2% in nine months of FY2026; the low-cost position claimed in the 2024 prospectus not repeated by the filer and not shown in the returns; the one quarter of volume gain not credited. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: a featured "free cash flow" with a $90M add-back and a ">25% adjusted FCF yield"; a "record third quarter" with a $20M net loss; CEO pay $9.79M in a year with a $159M net loss; FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance held by cutting planned capital spending by the $20M operating cash guidance fell; material weaknesses. Balance sheets of both predecessors read: Glatfelter's Specialty Papers sold 2018, $465M borrowed in 2021 for nonwovens purchases, $191M written off in 2022, equity 709 (2017) to 257 (2023) as debt rose to 854; Treasure debt-free with about $1.1B of goodwill and intangibles, then a $1,111M cash distribution to Berry at the merger, debt nil to $1.95B and equity halved; twelve-month interest about $151M against operating income about $63M. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (before interest, after stock pay and all capital spending, the predecessors combined) FY2021 to FY2025 $320M, $158.5M, $146M, $135M, $141M, average $180.1M, $145.2M without the COVID year FY2021, the central figure on the organic pair (the serial-acquirer test tripped by $13M); value range **$11.11 to $29.40** a share all-equity; fair price **negative on the all-equity basis ($(8.99))**, the midpoint at ten percent not covering $1,621M of net debt, **$4.29 equity-only**; no case earns ten percent at the price on the all-equity basis (best 8.9%); beside, not used, the twelve months to June 2026 alone (about $224M, capital spending $59M against depreciation about $144M) give $10.72; not armed. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's git status research-folder names and five commit subjects (KGHI, HLEO), file names in `Screens/_daily/` including the lock, one filtered `Test Runs/` listing for MAGN, GLT and Glatfelter returning nothing; none used. Commits 8e23c8bb (template), dc4464b3 (Step 0, balance sheets, foundations, Q1), ea37a2ef (Q2), a9993106 (box, facts after the stop, Q7 computation), 7a300146 (self-audit, framework gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 40 ids, no problem; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_verify.py`, 36 fragments within 300 characters before an id, 12 flags each read: 11 are filing quotes inside the window, **one near-slip**: the framework's own word "ordinary" in quotation marks beside **[M1999-108]**, whose row supports only the paraphrase that the moat is judged, not measured (framework wording beside an id, recorded, not fixed); no E-ids. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q2's commodity paragraph sends a business whose rivals' costs cannot be read to TOO HARD (NATURE) while the ordinary-returns item sends it OUT, the run applying the returns item; (2) the merger splice across a September and a December fiscal year under Q7(c); (3) the serial-acquirer test across a merger, purchases by the smaller predecessor, the line tripped by $13M; (4) Q7(a) when the filed combined series starts at the aberrational year; (5) a negative fair price, reported as none with the figure; (6) taxes a parent paid for a carve-out, deducted by a convention of the run; (7) a reused CIK, `tools/run.py` printing two companies as one series. Could not get: the rivals' unit costs; Treasure's full-year FY2024 organic volume (8-K/A exhibits are images); Glatfelter's October 2024; insider ownership; Mativ's filed statements (XBRL only).
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Magnera, NYSE MAGN, formerly Glatfelter; Berry Global's spun-off nonwovens business merged into Glatfelter on 2024-11-04 with a 1-for-13 reverse split; a commodity converter of nonwoven roll goods for a few large consumer-product makers: Americas, 83% of five-year segment profit, lost organic volume five years running and to imports in South America, customers can shift suppliers quickly on the filer's own words, the field's filers earned ordinary returns or less over a full cycle and the claimed low-cost position does not show in the returns. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: a featured free cash flow with a $90M add-back, a record quarter with a net loss, CEO pay of $9.79M in a $159M loss year, material weaknesses. Computation beneath the stop: value $11.11 to $29.40 all-equity, fair price negative all-equity ($(8.99)), $4.29 equity-only, not armed. One near-slip, framework wording beside an id. Framework gaps for the operator: Q2's commodity and ordinary-returns rules diverging when rivals do not file, a merger splice across fiscal years, the serial-acquirer test across a merger, a negative fair price, carve-out taxes, a reused CIK in tools/run.py.)
